plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks winning at a loss if my value is exceeded by the price I'd pay; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Since my value is $40, I will bid exactly $40 to ensure optimal expected profit.

In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of competitors' behavior. This is because your payment doesn't depend on your own bid (only on whether you win and the second-highest bid), so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding exactly my value of $13 maximizes expected profit: I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and pay only the second-highest, ensuring non-negative profit whenever I win.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding higher than my value risks overpaying, while bidding lower only risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior round history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid my true value of $17 to maximize expected profit.
